inspection_outcome: Four confirmed Major and eight Minor findings, with exact source version, counterevidence and repair limits retained.
summary: Four confirmed Major findings concern metric construction/descent, the formal zero-Lee theorem domain, the principal-torsor image criterion and the negative deformation class inference. Eight bounded Minor corrections remain; intended strict conclusions and repaired existence/openness results are not refuted.

problems.title: The positive-line metric and its finite arithmetic descent fail

source_claim.kind: definition, statement, construction or proof step
source_claim.location: Theorem2.4 converse, p9, norm-square potential and last displayed Omega_F identity
source_claim.claim: A positive-line norm-square gives a Vaisman metric and arithmetic averaging over the finite deck group equals the metric formed from the average Lee form.

problems.assumptions: Y=P1,L=O(1) positive FS,lambda in(0,1),P=Lx/<lambda> smooth compact definite elliptic bundle. For descent use free double cover E'=C/(Z+iZ)->E'/<z+1/2>, pullback of positive constant-curvature ample line, canonical order2 deck lift commuting with fiber G.
problems.counterexample: f=|w|²/(1+|z|²) has normalized complex Hessian diag(-1,1) at(0,1). For genuine normalized Vaisman theta±=theta0±epsilon d cos(2pi x), small epsilon, deck swaps them. Mean Omega=Omega0+epsilon²du wedge Jdu whereas formula from mean theta=Omega0. Its unique candidate Lee form k theta0 with k=omega0/(omega0+epsilon²du wedge Jdu) is not closed; actual mean is not LCK.
problems.counterevidence: Reciprocal norm or norm on negative dual supplies a valid metric; a NEW metric formed from average Lee form is positive and Vaisman. Neither construction counterexample disproves existence or headline strict Vaisman conclusions.
problems.impact: Major for actual central constructive direction and descent, which produce an indefinite form and a non-LCK average. Severity follows this core proof impact, not repair length or a requirement that the whole paper fail.
problems.correction: Use reciprocal positive-line potential with consistent normalization. Define new -dJtheta_F+theta_F wedge Jtheta_F, prove positivity from averaged transverse curvature/common vertical Lee field, and do not equate it with arithmetic metric mean.

check.independent_reasoning: The positive O(1) norm-squared potential has complex Hessian diag(-1,1) at (0,1). For the actual finite free deck example the arithmetic average is Omega0+epsilon^2 du wedge Jdu, not the metric reconstructed from the averaged Lee form; the candidate Lee factor k is nonconstant and nonclosed. Both failures lie in Theorem2.4's written construction. Negative-dual/reciprocal potential and a new form built from the averaged Lee form are genuine repairs, not counterexamples to existence.

problems.title: Printed Vaisman definition includes the excluded zero-Lee case

source_claim.kind: definition, statement, construction or proof step
source_claim.location: Intro pp1-2; Definition2.1 pp4-5; TheoremsB/C p2
source_claim.claim: Parallel closed Lee form alone defines Vaisman, while fixed Lee class/volume gives unique Ricci-flat metric and Aut0 has complex dimension1 when cBC<=0.

problems.assumptions: X=(C/Z[i])² complex dimension2; theta=0; c1=cBC1=0; positive flat metrics Omega_s=(i/2)(s dz1dbarz1+s^-1 dz2dbarz2),s>0.
problems.counterexample: All Omega_s satisfy the displayed definition, have identical Lee class0 and volume and Ricci0, yet are distinct. Aut0(X)=X has complex dimension2.
problems.counterevidence: Introduction explicitly concerns non-Kähler geometry; normalization norm(theta)=1 and one-dimensional Lee group show strict convention intended. n>1 is explicitly present and is not a finding.
problems.impact: Under the explicit printed definition, theta=0 is admitted and normalization is an optional additional condition. The flat complex two-torus family satisfies the written hypotheses and contradicts Theorem B(1) uniqueness and Theorem C dimension1. This is a Major formal theorem-domain defect. The non-Kahler motivation and one-dimensional Lee-group discussion support the intended strict convention, under which these examples are excluded; no counterexample to that restricted statement is asserted.
problems.correction: Require theta nonzero or explicitly define strict non-Kähler Vaisman throughout.

check.independent_reasoning: Root read the introductory and formal definitions on pp1-2 and4-5: dOmega=theta wedge Omega and parallel theta permit theta0; normalization is optional. The complex two-torus has a fixed-volume family of flat zero-Ricci metrics with identical Lee class0 and Aut0 complex dimension2. These violate the literal B1 uniqueness and C dimension assertions. Non-Kahler motivation and the Lee-group discussion are strong counterevidence for the intended strict convention, so the finding is expressly conditional on the explicit printed domain and does not refute the strict theorems.

problems.title: Proper locally free actions need compatible effective slice isotropy

source_claim.kind: definition, statement, construction or proof step
source_claim.location: Orbifold chart convention p5; Theorem2.2 p7
source_claim.claim: Every holomorphic proper locally free H-action has an effective orbifold quotient making its projection a principal H-orbibundle.

problems.assumptions: H=E=C/Z[i],K=<1/2>,X=(E/K)xP1, action induced by H->E/K. Compact complex dimension2, holomorphic proper action with finite stabilizerK.
problems.counterexample: Quotient is P1, generic effective orbifold stabilizer trivial, so generic principal H fiber must be E. Actual E/K has modulus2i, not SL2Z-equivalent to i since Im((ai+b)/(ci+d))=1/(c²+d²), never2.
problems.counterevidence: Actual Lee group is an effective abelian subgroup of AutX and has faithful slice isotropy; its intended application avoids this counterexample.
problems.impact: Broader quotient theorem false in stated generality; main Lee quotient remains available.
problems.correction: Require faithful local slice isotropy or explicitly allow ineffective orbifolds retaining generic isotropy. Do not confuse global effectiveness with slice effectiveness for a general H.

check.independent_reasoning: E acting on (E/K) times P1 through a finite nontrivial kernel is locally free but not an effective principal E action in the paper's effective-orbifold category. The actual Lee group is an effective subgroup of Aut(X), excluding this overbroad background case.

problems.title: Flat principal elliptic monodromy is incorrectly typed as group automorphisms

source_claim.kind: definition, statement, construction or proof step
source_claim.claim: The general zero-Chern principal difference bundle is associated to holomorphic group-automorphism monodromy, with a lifted C* representation.

problems.assumptions: Base and fiber E=G=C/Z[i]; total torus C²/lattice<(1,0),(i,sqrt2),(0,1),(0,i)>; Chern0, translation monodromy.
problems.counterexample: A continuous section w=sqrt2 Imz proves topological triviality. A holomorphic section would have affine liftaz+b with a in Z[i] and ia-sqrt2 in Z[i], impossible. Aut_gp transitions have zero section and are principal-translation-equivariant only ifidentity. Tensor with positive line-induced bundle embeds example in the positive Chern image criterion.
problems.counterevidence: Exact exponential sheaf sequences prove the desired image criterion directly: zero-Chern P0 comes fromu inH1(O), whose image inH1(O*) maps toP0.
problems.impact: The false group-automorphism suspension and unsupported lift prove the inverse psi_* image criterion on p9. The same page invokes that discussion to construct q*P in Theorem2.4. The nonsplit translation bundle can be combined with a positive line-induced bundle in the actual definite case. This invalid core construction warrants Major; the common H1(O) class provides a valid new sheaf-theoretic repair, not a counterexample to the image criterion itself.
problems.correction: Use the common H1(O) element in the commuting exponential sequences; if discussing monodromy, use translationsG and justify any lift.

check.independent_reasoning: The torus extension with periods (1,0),(i,sqrt2),(0,1),(0,i) has vanishing topological Chern class but no holomorphic section: its lifted derivative is constant a and the two lattice conditions contradict irrational sqrt2. Group-automorphism suspension fixes zero and cannot represent this translation torsor. Tensoring a positive line-induced bundle puts the obstruction in the actual definite case. Root directly read p9 and verified the dependence of Theorem2.4 on the inverse image criterion. The common H1(O) class in the two exponential sequences is a valid replacement.
